value.body: Surveyors measure land and sites to produce maps, levels and layouts for construction and land records. They work for construction firms, survey agencies, infrastructure projects and government departments, and the day is spent in the field with instruments and then processing the data on a computer.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Civil Engineering B.Tech or diploma; ITI surveyor trade for field roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Total station, auto level, GPS / DGPS, AutoCAD, drone survey software

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as survey engineers on construction or infrastructure projects, or with survey agencies. Hands-on practice with a total station and AutoCAD is the main thing employers look for.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Operating a total station, level and GPS

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is mostly outdoors and on project sites.
Common next steps: senior surveyor, survey manager, GIS or drone-mapping roles.
Drone and GPS-based surveying are changing how field work is done.
